nodes.name: write_user_audit_log
nodes.description: NEW since the last mapping run. Single shared writer for user-targeted entries in the admin_audit_log collection, extracted because that collection already received hand-built documents from four independent call sites (deployment_settings_service.update, the organizations modules-update endpoint, admin.py's mfa_reset, the genetics cascade-purge/orphan-sweep routes). Writes the canonical shape: action (dotted, e.g. 'user.role.changed'), targetUserId, targetUserEmail, performedBy (userId, or 'system:<name>' for server-initiated actions with no HTTP actor), performedByEmail, performedByRole (UserRole enum normalised to its string value), tz-aware UTC timestamp, and a details dict carrying before/after. Deliberately never raises: a DB/logging failure is logged with exc_info and swallowed so an audit-write failure can never surface as a failure of the already-committed action it records. Called by core.service.user_service (role change / activate / deactivate), core.api.admin, and src/main.py's seed_admin path.

nodes.name: label_printer_service
nodes.description: NEW since the last mapping run (T-925). HTTP client for a Brother QL-800 network print agent, called by the genetics label routes. Configuration is NOT read from settings directly — all three managed keys (LABEL_PRINTER_ENABLED / LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL / LABEL_PRINTER_API_KEY) are resolved fresh on every call via deployment_settings_service.get_value (env -> db -> unset), so a super_admin toggling the printer or rotating the key takes effect within that service's 30s cache window. health() never raises — unconfigured/unreachable/timeout/non-2xx/unparseable all collapse to a structured PrinterHealthResult so GET /genetics/printer/health can always return 200; `configured=False` means 'no printer set up here', distinct from ok=False meaning 'printer is broken'. print_pdf() preflights /health and refuses unless status == ['ready'] (the printer's spooler silently discards jobs when disconnected, so HTTP 200 is not evidence a label came out), enforces copies 1..50, and maps failures to 409 (not configured), 422 (bad input, printer's own message passed through), 502 (not ready / API key rejected / spooler problem / unreachable). Retries a 502 at most once per the printer contract. The X-API-Key header is sent only to the configured base URL and is never logged (log lines name only the exception type, never its message).

nodes.name: deployment_settings_service
nodes.description: Resolves and updates deployment-wide config held in the platform_settings singleton doc, so a super_admin can change it from the browser without an .env edit + container restart. Resolution order per key: env var (if set and non-empty) -> DB value -> unset; env acts as a LOCK, reporting source='env', editable=False. 12 managed keys: PUBLIC_BASE_URL, FRONTEND_URL, the CF_ACCESS_* block (ENABLED/TEAM_DOMAIN/AUD/EXCLUSIVE/JIT_PROVISION/DEFAULT_ROLE), and — added by T-925 — LABEL_PRINTER_ENABLED, LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL, LABEL_PRINTER_API_KEY (consumed by core.service.label_printer_service). Secret tier (_SECRET_KEYS: CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN, CF_ACCESS_AUD, LABEL_PRINTER_API_KEY) is never returned in full — isSet + last-4 masked hint only, masked in the audit log too; there is deliberately no reveal endpoint. update() enforces six guardrails: (a) CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN validated against Cloudflare's JWKS before persisting, (b) CF_ACCESS_EXCLUSIVE blocked until a CF Access sign-in has actually succeeded here (anti-lockout), (c) the acting super_admin's current password re-verified, (d) every changed key written to admin_audit_log with masked before/after, (e) LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL must parse as an http(s) URL with a host (422 otherwise — bounds the SSRF surface this key opens), (f) LABEL_PRINTER_ENABLED cannot flip to True unless a base URL AND API key are already resolved (same PATCH or already stored), so enabling it can never produce a runtime 500 on first print. 30s in-process cache (time.monotonic) because get_value is on the auth hot path. Sole writer of platform_settings.

nodes.name: email utilities
nodes.description: STUB, not a real mailer. All three senders build a link off settings.FRONTEND_URL and, when ENVIRONMENT == 'development', log the full message body to the application log and return True; in every other environment they fall through to a commented-out SendGrid example and still return True. No SMTP/SES/SendGrid integration exists, so on a non-development deployment verification and password-reset emails are silently never delivered while the caller sees success. Imported by core.service.auth_service for the register / send-verification / request-password-reset flows.

nodes.name: password hashing + JWT helpers
nodes.description: Cryptographic primitives shared by every auth path: passlib/bcrypt password hashing and verification, plus python-jose HS256 token minting/verification for the four token kinds (access, refresh, email-verification/password-reset, pending-MFA). Keyed off settings.SECRET_KEY. Imported by core.service.auth_service, core.service.deployment_settings_service (verify_password for the guardrail-c password re-check), and core.middleware.auth.

nodes.name: Fernet encryption helpers
nodes.description: Symmetric encryption-at-rest helpers built on Fernet with a PBKDF2-derived key. Three separately-named encrypt/decrypt pairs (module license keys, SenseHub device passwords, Telegram bot tokens) plus hash_license_key for lookup without decryption and a self-test roundtrip. Imported by core.service.module_manager for license-key storage.

nodes.name: LicenseValidator
nodes.description: Validates module license keys before a module is allowed to install. ValidationMode selects between local (HMAC signature check) and remote validation-server modes; generate_test_license produces development keys. Consumed only by core.service.module_manager.install_module.

nodes.name: FRONTEND_URL
nodes.description: Base URL of the user-facing SPA (default 'http://localhost:3000'), used to build the links embedded in verification / password-reset emails (src/utils/email.py). Managed key: resolution order env -> platform_settings DB -> unset, editable via PATCH /admin/deployment-settings when not env-pinned.

nodes.name: LABEL_PRINTER_ENABLED
nodes.description: T-925. Master switch for Brother QL-800 network label printing (default False). Unset/false makes core.service.label_printer_service refuse to print rather than fire a request at an empty base URL. Cannot be flipped True via PATCH /admin/deployment-settings unless LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL and LABEL_PRINTER_API_KEY are both already resolved (guardrail f in deployment_settings_service.update).

nodes.name: LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL
nodes.description: T-925. Full http(s) URL including port of the deployment's print agent, e.g. 'http://<printer-host>:8765' (default '' — deliberately no default, since a wrong one would point every deployment's print jobs AND its API key at somebody else's printer). Validated on write by deployment_settings_service._validate_label_printer_base_url (must parse as http/https with a host, 422 otherwise), which bounds the SSRF surface this key opens.

nodes.name: LABEL_PRINTER_API_KEY
nodes.description: T-925. Secret-tier managed key (default ''), sent as the X-API-Key header on every request to LABEL_PRINTER_BASE_URL and nowhere else. Treated exactly like CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN/CF_ACCESS_AUD: never logged, never returned in full by GET /admin/deployment-settings (isSet + last-4 masked hint only), masked in admin_audit_log, and there is deliberately no reveal endpoint.

nodes.name: users
nodes.description: Primary account collection. Indexes declared by MongoDBManager._create_indexes: unique email, unique userId, role, createdAt desc. Also carries the live MFA state inline (mfaSecret, mfaBackupCodes, mfaPendingSecret, mfaLastUsedCounter) rather than in the separate user_mfa collection, plus defaultDivisionId (set by division select), organizationId, authProvider and nameAutoDerived. Written by auth_service, user_service, mfa_service and division_service; read by deployment_settings_service for the guardrail-c password check.

nodes.name: refresh_tokens
nodes.description: Issued refresh tokens for rotation and revocation. Indexes: unique tokenId, userId, and a TTL index on expiresAt so expired rows self-delete. Written by auth_service (issue/rotate/logout) and user_service (revoke-all on deactivate/delete).

nodes.name: verification_tokens
nodes.description: One-time tokens for email verification and password reset. Indexes: unique tokenId, userId, email, tokenType, plus a TTL index on expiresAt. Written and consumed by auth_service.

nodes.name: mfa_pending_tokens
nodes.description: Short-lived challenge tokens issued when a password login succeeds but MFA is still required; POST /auth/mfa/verify exchanges one for the real token pair. Created and consumed entirely inside auth_service (_issue_mfa_challenge / verify path) — note this collection is NOT declared in MongoDBManager._create_indexes, so it carries no indexes and no TTL.

nodes.name: admin_audit_log
nodes.description: Append-only trail of privileged actions: user-targeted admin actions (role change, activate/deactivate, forced MFA reset) via core.service.audit_log_service, deployment-settings changes with masked before/after via deployment_settings_service.update, tenant module toggles from the organizations endpoint, and the genetics cascade-purge / orphan-sweep routes. Every writer is best-effort — none rolls back the mutation if the audit insert fails.

nodes.name: organizations
nodes.description: Top-level tenancy unit (unique slug). Holds the Wave 0 per-tenant modules sub-document: modules.financeEnabled (hides the Finance UI and gates the finance_bridge outbox writer) and modules.publicInfoPage (T-804 privacy config for scanned genetics labels). Written by organization_service; read by finance_bridge.tenant_flag and genetics.api.public.

nodes.name: divisions
nodes.description: Divisions scoped to an organization, each mapped to an IndustryType (vegetable_fruits / mushroom) and carrying a divisionCode unique per org. The divisionId here is what core.repository_base.DivisionScopedRepository auto-injects into every scoped query. Written by division_service.

nodes.name: installed_modules
nodes.description: Registry of Docker-Compose-installed modules. Indexes: unique module_name, status, health, installed_by_user_id, installed_at desc, updated_at desc, container_id. Written exclusively by core.service.module_manager.

nodes.name: module_audit_log
nodes.description: Audit trail for module install/uninstall/status operations. Indexes: module_name, operation, user_id, status, timestamp desc, plus a 90-day TTL index on timestamp. Written by core.service.module_manager, surfaced by GET /modules/audit-log.

nodes.name: port_registry
nodes.description: Allocation table for the 9001-19999 module port range. Indexes created by PortManager itself (not by MongoDBManager): unique port, module_name, status, and a compound (module_name, status). Written only by core.service.port_manager, which rolls back partial allocations on failure.

nodes.name: user_mfa
nodes.description: DECLARED BUT UNUSED. MongoDBManager._create_indexes builds indexes here (unique mfaId, unique userId, isEnabled, createdAt/updatedAt desc) and src/models/mfa.py defines a matching schema, but core.service.mfa_service keeps all live MFA state inline on the users document instead. Nothing reads or writes this collection today — it is a parallel/legacy design that was indexed but never wired up.

nodes.name: mfa_backup_codes
nodes.description: DECLARED BUT UNUSED, same story as user_mfa. Indexes exist (unique codeId, userId, (userId, codeHash), isUsed, (userId, isUsed), TTL) but mfa_service stores the 10 SHA-256-hashed backup codes on the users document.

nodes.name: mfa_audit_log
nodes.description: DECLARED BUT UNUSED, same story as user_mfa / mfa_backup_codes. Indexed by MongoDBManager (unique logId, ...) but no code path writes it; MFA-related admin actions land in admin_audit_log instead.
